science.title: Meet the ‘celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness’
science.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03750-4Astronomers report a rare pair of extremely bright black holes that were gobbling gas less than one billion years after the Big Bang.

science.title: Dinosaur’s rest break leaves a lasting impression
science.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03749-xA fossilized print records marks left by the feet and bum of a juvenile reptile that measured one metre at the hip.

science.title: The origins of scrotal asymmetry
science.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03279-6Why does the left testicle tend to hang lower than the right? And a small village with a surprisingly ambitious museum, in our weekly dip into Nature’s archive.

science.title: Is academia’s risk-averse culture stifling scientific discovery?
science.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03772-yFear of failure can cause researchers to stay within their comfort zone, impacting innovation, argues Nessa Carey.

science.title: The world’s most precious brain samples — and what they teach us about being human
science.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03711-xHow do human neurons behave in their natural environment? To answer that question, you need rare brain samples taken from living humans — and very steady hands.

science.title: Measles is back in the US: what worries scientists
science.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03747-zOutbreak in the United States that has killed both adults and children increases risk of spread to other countries.

science.title: The prospect of a ‘super’ El Niño demands better ocean monitoring
science.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03744-2The prospect of a ‘super’ El Niño demands better ocean monitoring

science.title: How measuring the state of nature can reverse biodiversity loss
science.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03714-8A collective effort by governments, communities and businesses to track the impacts of conservation and restoration is essential to maintaining nature and the services it provides.

science.title: Turning biomass into renewable fuels and chemicals using microorganisms
science.summary: Texas A&M University researchers have developed a process that converts biomass into renewable fuels and chemicals. Dr. Mark Holtzapple, professor in the Artie McFerrin Department of Chemical Engineering, aims to make producing these products more efficient and affordable by using microorganisms to break down plant material.

science.title: Ultracold diamond microwave laser amplifies quantum signals 1,000-fold
science.summary: Researchers from the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST) have created a spin-based microwave amplifier that operates near absolute zero, boosting signals by more than 1,000-fold while adding noise close to the bare minimum required by the laws of physics.
